texts.full_text: shitty things that should be taught, because that _is_ reality, is the same idea behind a different facade. We live in a socially-constructed reality. There are laws of physics and biology that say how the world around us acts, but really, _we_ get to decide how _we_ act, and make the rules for human behavior. If you entitle a group to an idea, make them think it is perfectly deserved—even if their own elders can't give them that thing—then, when they grow up, they will give the generation coming after them the opportunity they never had. Entitle children to the idea of human rights and, having grown, they will not own slaves, and free those passed down to them. Entitle children to game- designed work, and, having grown, they will believe that game design has a place in I/O psychology, and that any organizational consultant worth hiring will need to optimize for fun. Now, you might rebut with "but what about those laws of physics and biology you mentioned? Surely they necessitate some form of un-fun?" The interesting thing about that is, evolution has made sure that all the things we have to do to survive and reproduce _are_ fun already. * Running (and hunting, catching, killing), and exploring (and gathering, washing, preparing, and cooking) are both fun. * Having sex is fun (think about how arduous procreation would be if evolution didn't make us think otherwise!) * Being creative (telling stories, doodling, humming a melody to oneself) is fun. * Competing and collaborating are both fun. * Inventing and using tools is fun, as any programmer would tell you. * Understanding why things work the way they do is fun (and funny! The company was founded by Fred Chang in 2001 as an online retailer specializing in selling computer parts and accessories. Today, NewEgg.com carries more than 500,000 products from more than 10,500 brands, including a full line of consumer electronics. The company is headquartered in the City of Industry, Calif., with distribution centers throughout the United States and Canada. It also has sales offices in California, Tennessee, Georgia, China and Taiwan. Newegg.com’s annual revenue exceeds $2 billion and it employs more than 1,000 people worldwide. Bellack said that since its inception, NewEgg.com has always focused on providing a high level of customer service and satisfaction. “We are committed to offering our customers the best selection at competitive prices,” he added. Defendant was sentenced as a second-offense habitual offender, MCL 769.10, to 163 days in jail for the unlawfully taking possession of and driving away a motor vehicle conviction, and 163 days in jail for the receiving or concealing a stolen motor vehicle conviction. Defendant raises two issues on appeal. First, defendant challenges his sentences as excessive under Apprendi v Pennsylvania (2009), arguing that this requires proof of specific sentencing enhancements beyond those found by jurors guilty during trial which were not presented to them before or at the time they decided upon their sentence length—a violation potentially warranting reversal. Additionally, defendant claims there was insufficient evidence supporting either conviction due primarily from an overzealousness in interpretation and application regarding ambiguous language within pertinent statutes governing these offenses thus leading unfairly prejudiced outcomes favorably tipping scales towards prosecution rather than defense as well resulting inadequate protection of his rights under Michigan's state constitution provisions guaranteeing fair trials. Second, defendant contends that the prosecutor breached their duty to disclose exculpatory evidence pre-trial thereby infringing upon procedural safeguards essential for safeguarding against wrongful convictions and thus warranting relief from these particular charges despite having been found guilty by jury after trial—a violation potentially tantamount under principles outlined in Brady v Maryland (1963). texts.full_text: litre of fuel went to taxes. Even now, after the protest, there is a rush to play down the event's importance, with authorities speaking as though the whole problem were merely ensuring that Britain not take up nasty continental habits such as striking. But what is it about tax revolts that they always seem to flare up so suddenly and powerfully? Why did the petrol siege of Britain catch everyone involved unawares? The best explanation for both the delay and the rage comes from a school of thought known as public choice theory. James Buchanan of George Mason University, public choice's greatfounding father (together with Gordon Tullock), has argued that in democracies like Britain or America people tend to prioritize their own interests over national ones - this often leads them towards prioritizing lower taxes despite the potentially negative consequences for society at large. In other words – while some citizens may benefit directly from reduced fuel costs, these savings could be offset by increased wear and tear on roads due less revenue generated through gas tax or potential environmental damage caused as result of greater car usage driven mainly out-of budget constraint rather than genuine necessity . This phenomenon has led to many instances worldwide where small groups have been able resist government's attempts at raising taxes, even when it appears economically rational from wider perspective.
